To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the radiation-induced lung changes are not dose dependent and are not the cause of the death of irradiated rabbits; that the spinal cord lesions are dose dependent, and that the dose required to produce spinal cord damage is much higher for neutrons than for photons; and that the dose of neutrons required to induce malignant tumors in bone is about 2.5 times that for photons.

the pathologic effects of fast neutrons are similar to the pathologic effects produced by photons of equivalent dose, and that both photon and neutron irradiation produce lung damage that is similar in character but different in timing.

(1) the spinal cord is more sensitive to neutron irradiation than is the lung and (2) lung changes in rabbits irradiated with fast neutrons are not more severe or more likely to lead to respiratory distress than those produced by equivalent doses of photons.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pathologic effects of neutrons and photons on rabbit spinal cord are similar, and that neutrons are more effective than photons in producing pulmonary and bone lesions.
the effects of neutrons and photons on the lung and spinal cords of the rabbits studied were essentially similar, except for the greater frequency of spinal cord lesions after high neutron doses.
the pathologic changes in the spinal cord are much more serious than those in the lung, and that the spinal cord is the critical organ in these experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spinal cord is more resistant than the lung to radiation injury, and that the pathologic effects of fast neutrons and photons are similar.
, although neutrons were more effective than photons in causing paraplegia, they were no more effective than photons for inducing lung changes, and were less effective for producing bone tumors.

the pathologic effects of fast neutrons in the lung were similar to those of photons, but that the pathologic response in the spinal cord to neutrons was much greater than that to photons, and that the pathologic changes in both organs were more severe when the dose rate was high.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fast neutrons can cause severe radiation-induced lung changes and malignant bone tumors, and that they can cause paraplegia and severe radiation myelopathy in rabbits.

fast neutron irradiation of the spinal cord of rabbits is more effective than photon irradiation in producing paralysis, and that spinal cord damage can be produced in rabbits by fast neutron doses as small as 2520 rad.

the pathologic effects of neutrons on the lung and spinal are not different from those of X-rays, and that radiation-induced lung changes may be more important in the pathogenesis of radiation-induced spinal cord lesions than has been generally believed.
